title: Club owners and the union's weakness today
summary: Clubs in the Quarter are run by Italian owners and managers, union scale is rarely paid, and higher scale cost bands a front-line player.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: But most of the clubs in the quarter or in that area aren't?
They're run by those people who's in cahoots with one or another, you know.
In what way? How do you mean?

I mean, you know, Italian people usually run things down there. You know, I don't know who, I don't say they're the mafia, but the people who were running things, you know. Several of them have died out. The place where I was, at least two or three of them have died, you know.
Yeah, the owners have died. Who were fronting for the owners or whatever it was.

Managers. Because right now this lady, Ms. Matabano, she's running things over there now. When her husband died, Carlos, Carlos Matabano, after he died, then she brought the other people out who was ever into the stuff, you know. So everything seemed to be under her control. So Ms. Steve Valenti at the Paddock Lounge, you know, she was renting from this other lady that on, what's that woman's name? She used to, every Easter she'd be in the Easter Parade.
Not Brazil, Brazil, whatever her name, I can't think of her name.

But she used to rent the place on a yearly basis to Ms. Valenti. She did it for years. But after Ms. Valenti died, then she kept the place for a while, and then later on they converted to something else. Sousa, what that man named? John Sousa, with the Dukes of Dixeland, I think they went in there.
John Shoup, yeah. John Shoup. They converted to a... I don't know what it is down there now.
Is the union not coming in and being strict with the clubs? Is that the problem?

They don't seem to have any power to do anything, man. It's just there now. I don't see that they're doing too much of anything. I don't think the union is too powerful down here anyway. I don't see that they're doing anything. They're just telling the few people that are still in it, you can make this, you can make that. Because when they went up on the scale, they would drop either a trombone player or a clarinet player.

Because once upon a time, they had the front line, you had trumpet, trombone, clarinet. And then you had the rhythm in the back there, banjo, piano, bass, and drums. They went up on the scale, they dropped somebody, either a clarinet player or a trombone player. Yeah.
